title: Elastic Cycle Mesh: slotting, staff glidepaths, and emergency descope protocol
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: As Redwood scales across hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes, we need a deterministic, low-friction approach to assign engineering and cross-functional capacity into repeating cycles. Current practice relies on ad hoc negotiations and per-team heuristics, which leads to uneven coverage of mission-critical runway (runtime improvements, reliability SLOs, and enterprise readiness).

Objective: Create an operational playbook — the "Elastic Cycle Mesh" — that prescribes (1) a slotting algorithm for allocation of team capacity across focus lanes, (2) role-level glidepaths for predictable staffing handoffs and shadowing, and (3) an emergency descope protocol for mid-cycle shocks. This playbook should reduce planning friction, improve predictability for PM/Eng/Design, and provide clear communications steps for scope cuts.

Scope: This ticket covers the playbook design, a lightweight slotting rubric, staffing glidepath templates (owner/backup/mentor for key roles), communication templates for scope cuts, and a set of acceptance criteria and KPIs to measure adoption. Implementation (tooling or automation) will be a follow-on ticket in the cycle capacity roadmap.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change hiring plans, compensation, or create automated tooling for enforcing slotting. It does not rework the org structure or touch payroll.

Key definitions:
- Slot: a contiguous commitment window (two-week default) of effort assigned to an initiative lane (e.g., runtime-performance, dedicated-capacity, private-deploy).
- Glidepath: the plan for who owns a slot over time, including primary owner, shadow/backup, and a short handoff checklist.
- Emergency descope: a fast, governed process to reduce scope when cross-team capacity shock occurs (e.g., incident, hiring freeze, unexpected customer escalations).

Proposed approach:
1) Slotting rubric: each initiative gets slots based on a three-factor score: business criticality (40%), execution risk (30%), and cross-team dependency surface (30%). Translate scores to slot counts per cycle using a normalized table. Use a default 30% multi-sprint buffer for cross-cutting infra work.

2) Role glidepaths: define three templates by initiative size: small (1 slot, single owner + mentor), medium (2-3 slots, owner + backup + shadow), large (4+ slots, owner cohort + rotation schedule). Each template includes a 3-point handoff checklist: objectives, open risks & mitigations, and test/runbook pointers (links).

3) Emergency descope protocol: fast triage meeting (15-30m) chaired by PM lead + Eng lead, a decision matrix (must vs nice-to-have), and a pre-authorized fallback assignment of buffer slots. Communication responsibilities: PM drafts customer message, Eng drafts rollback/feature-toggle plan, Design drafts in-product messaging. Keep a one-line log in the cycle playbook and a follow-up retro within five working days.

4) Communication & tooling hygiene: canonical playbook lives in Confluence (link placeholder), slot table is a Google sheet for the cycle and a read-only export to the Console roadmap tab for visibility. Include a template PRD section called "Cycle Slot Summary" to standardize handoffs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook document created and reviewed by Eng, Design, SRE, and GTM leads.
- Slotting rubric validated on three upcoming initiatives and an allocation table published for the next cycle.
- Glidepath templates adopted by at least two squads during the pilot cycle.
- Emergency descope protocol executed in a simulated drill within the pilot cycle and documented.

KPIs (pilot cycle):
- Planning friction score (survey) reduced by 30% from baseline.
- Percentage of initiatives with a documented glidepath >= 80%.
- Time to decision during simulated emergency descope <= 30 minutes.

Deliverables:
- Confluence playbook (canonical) with scoring rubric and templates (deliverable link: Confluence/Playbooks/Cycle-Mesh).
- Slot allocation spreadsheet for the pilot cycle.
- Email/Slack templates for scope-cut announcements and customer comms.
- After-action retro note capturing lessons and improvement actions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Overly prescriptive rubric sparks pushback. Mitigation: include a discretionary buffer and a quick appeals process (PM council).
- Risk: Teams treat glidepaths as a checkbox. Mitigation: require a short sync during sprint planning and include glidepath compliance in the cycle review.

Next steps:
- Draft playbook and circulate to cross-functional WG (SRE, Eng leads, Design, Solutions Eng) by 2026-03-05.
- Run a calibration session with leads to score three pilot initiatives by 2026-03-12.
- Publish pilot slot allocations and glidepath assignments by 2026-03-17.
